summary: Backend-only testing of the Resend email integration for aftersales.pro. Created /app/backend/tests/test_email_integration.py (19 pytest cases, all PASSED) covering POST /api/auth/forgot-password (valid user, unknown email, unknown subdomain, validation 422s, email-send attempt logged), POST /api/auth/reset-password (invalid token, short password, full E2E signup -> forgot -> token from DB -> reset -> login with new password -> old password rejected -> token reuse blocked), POST /api/tenants/signup (welcome + admin new-signup alert email triggers), POST /api/super-admin/trigger-email-checks (401 unauth, 403 with tenant token, 200 success as super admin), background scheduler startup log, and email_service module/template unit checks. Additionally proved real end-to-end delivery: sending to the Resend-verified account address (aftersales@thegoodmen.in) returned {'success': True, 'email_id': '3bd487e8-...'}. All other recipients fail only with the expected Resend domain-verification / test-mode error, which is correctly caught and logged. No 500s observed; all endpoints behave as specified.

critical.issue: Inactive-reminder emails can NEVER be sent. The query filters on users.last_login_at, but `last_login_at` is never written anywhere in server.py (POST /api/auth/login does not update it). grep confirms the field only appears in this query. Feature is effectively dead code.

Reset link is hardcoded to https://aftersales.pro/reset-password?token=... (server.py:1182). In preview/staging the emailed link points at production, so the reset flow cannot be completed from this environment. Should be built from an env var (e.g. FRONTEND_URL); no such key exists in backend/.env. Same hardcoding at lines 7213, 7249, 7280, 7313.

minor.issue: Returns HTTP 200 with {'status':'error'} on internal failure instead of 500 — failures are invisible to monitoring/clients.

No dedup guard (unlike check_inactive_users which uses email_reminders). The scheduler runs immediately on every app startup and backend hot-reloads restart the app frequently, so trial-ending / subscription-expired emails will be re-sent to the same tenant multiple times per day. Confirmed multiple 'Running scheduled email tasks...' entries within minutes in backend.err.log.

No rate limiting and no invalidation of previously issued unused tokens; repeated calls create unlimited password_resets rows and repeated emails (email-bombing vector). No index on password_resets.token / expires_at TTL.
No persistence/audit of send results (no email_logs collection); only logger output, so delivery failures are unqueryable from the app/admin UI.

asyncio.create_task(...) results are never awaited or referenced, so tasks may be garbage-collected before completion and exceptions inside them are only visible via email_service's own logger. Consider FastAPI BackgroundTasks or keeping a task set.

SENDER_EMAIL defaults to onboarding@resend.dev; all real tenant emails currently fail with 'You can only send testing emails to your own email address (aftersales@thegoodmen.in)'. A verified sending domain must be configured before launch (expected per request, flagged for release readiness).

action_items: Set users.last_login_at on POST /api/auth/login (and super-admin login) so check_inactive_users actually finds inactive tenants.
Add FRONTEND_URL / APP_BASE_URL to backend/.env and use it to build reset/billing/login links instead of hardcoded https://aftersales.pro/... (server.py 1182, 7213, 7249, 7280, 7313).
Add dedup records (like email_reminders) for trial-ending and subscription-expired emails, and avoid running the daily job immediately on every startup/hot-reload.
Make POST /api/super-admin/trigger-email-checks return 500 on failure instead of 200 + status:error.
Add rate limiting to /api/auth/forgot-password and invalidate prior unused reset tokens; add TTL/index on password_resets.
Optional: log every send attempt to an email_logs collection for auditability; remove unused imports send_milestone_email / send_weekly_summary (imported but never called).
critical_code_review_comments: check_inactive_users depends on a field (last_login_at) that no code writes — dead feature.
Hardcoded production URLs inside email bodies break the reset flow in non-production environments.
server.py is 7369 lines; email background tasks/schedulers and super-admin routes should be split into separate modules.
@app.on_event('startup')/'shutdown') is deprecated in current FastAPI; asynccontextmanager is already imported but unused — migrate to lifespan.
Fire-and-forget asyncio.create_task without holding a reference risks task GC; also duplicate 'import asyncio' inside functions while it is already imported at module level.
seed_data_creation: Created and deleted two temporary tenants (subdomains testreset<hex>, testwel<hex>) with TEST_-prefixed admin emails; associated users/branches/password_resets removed in test teardown. One real probe email sent to aftersales@thegoodmen.in.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_email_integration.py -v`. Resend API key is valid and delivery works ONLY to aftersales@thegoodmen.in (account owner) until a domain is verified; every other recipient logs 'Failed to send email to X: You can only send testing emails...' or 'Invalid `to` field' for example.com addresses — tests assert on the send ATTEMPT log, not success. Backend logs are in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log. Razorpay-webhook-triggered emails (payment success/failed/renewed, server.py 7100-7215) were NOT tested because they require a valid webhook HMAC signature; test them with a signed payload using RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Inactive-reminder path cannot be verified until last_login_at is populated.
rca_of_the_issue: All requested endpoints function correctly. The two high-priority findings are logic gaps rather than runtime errors: (1) check_inactive_users queries users.last_login_at which is never set by the login endpoint, so the inactive-reminder lifecycle email will never fire; (2) email link URLs are hardcoded to the production domain, so password-reset links emailed from preview/staging are unusable. Email delivery failures observed during testing are purely Resend test-mode domain-verification restrictions (verified by a successful send to the account-owner address returning a Resend email_id), and are caught and logged correctly by email_service.send_email.
